    From the squeezeless sponge to the block sponge (EasyCrypt proof/smart_counter/Gconcl_list.ec) #

    — EC-fidelity port

    EC's judgments in EC's scripts, over the old port's declarations (section FirstPort below), as SmartCounter/Gconcl.lean. The plain lemmas (leq_add_nin, …) are the old port's.

    Translation:

    • EC's local equiv E (D <: DISTINGUISHER {-…}) : … is a theorem ∀ (D <: DISTINGUISHER {-…}), equiv[ … ].

    Declarations of the first port #

    Definitions and plain lemmas of the first port of this file (2026-10/11) that the proofs below use; its program-logic proofs are gone.

    The first port's translation notes (some mention declarations that went with its proofs):

    • op valid = valid_block (as a test) and the axioms on parse and format are the parameter class Params (over BlockSponge.Params).
    • Both SLCommon and BlockSponge define C, DRestr, DISTINGUISHER …; as in EasyCrypt (where BlockSponge is imported last), the unqualified names are BlockSponge's, and SLCommon's are written SLCommon.X.
    • The clones BIRO2 (of IRO), F2 (of SLCommon's F) declare their own module variables; the section's local IRO2 (of PROM.FullRO) has its variable as a lens parameter of the local declarations, fresh by hypothesis (exception E6).
    • SLCommon's and BlockSponge's PRIMITIVE/DPRIMITIVE are one module type in EasyCrypt (they depend on state only); in Lean their instances differ, so a module passing one as the other repackages it with mk (A's P).
    • Local modules that alias a procedure of an applied functor (L3) are Lean functions returning that procedure (the port's IF', Valid2, D2, D3, D5, D6 are modules with procedure aliases, proc f = c;; its L, L2, L4 are abbrevs). SimLast's and DValid's aliases are EC's too (proc f = c;); S2(F) = S(Last(F)), a whole-module alias whose PRIMITIVE is SLCommon's, is a module of its own with S(Last(F))'s procedures as aliases (exception E5).

        @[simp]
        theorem GaudisCrypt.SHA3.Gconcl_list.DSqueeze.apply_simp [SLCommon.Params] [BlockSponge.Params] [Params] (F : SLCommon.DFUNCTIONALITY) :
        Module.app DSqueeze F = Module.pair init (Module.app f F)

        @[simp]: applying DSqueeze to a tuple of its single parameter F — the record of its procedures DSqueeze.init, DSqueeze.f, each applied to the parameters it uses.

        This is the lemma that unfolds a module use: simp rewrites with it, then with the field lemmas of the module type (N.f.mk_simp) to get at the one procedure the goal is about, and then with DSqueeze.init.apply_simp, DSqueeze.f.apply_simp to fill that procedure's holes.

        The body of proc init of module DSqueeze, as a procedure of its own: it calls no module parameter, so it has no holes.

        A hole stands for a call whose callee is not known here — a module parameter is supplied only when the module is applied — so the body is a ProcedureWithHoles, to be instantiated (see DSqueeze.init.procedure.apply_simp) rather than run. Use DSqueeze.init for this procedure as a module.

                                                @[simp]
                                                theorem GaudisCrypt.SHA3.Gconcl_list.Valid.apply_simp [SLCommon.Params] [BlockSponge.Params] [Params] (F : DFUNCTIONALITY) :
                                                Module.app Valid F = Module.pair init (Module.app f F)

                                                @[simp]: applying Valid to a tuple of its single parameter F — the record of its procedures Valid.init, Valid.f, each applied to the parameters it uses.

                                                This is the lemma that unfolds a module use: simp rewrites with it, then with the field lemmas of the module type (N.f.mk_simp) to get at the one procedure the goal is about, and then with Valid.init.apply_simp, Valid.f.apply_simp to fill that procedure's holes.

                                                source
                                                @[simp]
                                                theorem GaudisCrypt.SHA3.Gconcl_list.Valid.f.apply_simp [SLCommon.Params] [BlockSponge.Params] [Params] (F : DFUNCTIONALITY) :
                                                Module.app f F = Module.proc (procedure.instantiate (Indifferentiability.DFUNCTIONALITY.f state (List Common.block × ℤ) (List Common.block) F).procedure)

                                                @[simp]: applying Valid.f to the parameters proc f uses (F) is Module.proc (Valid.f.procedure.instantiate …) — the procedure with its holes filled by the callees they were made from, each written as it was in the body (with the arguments in place of the module parameters) and turned into a Procedure by Module.Proc.procedure.

                                                The body of proc f of module Valid, as a procedure of its own: the one call it makes to a module parameter (F) is its single hole.

                                                A hole stands for a call whose callee is not known here — a module parameter is supplied only when the module is applied — so the body is a ProcedureWithHoles, to be instantiated (see Valid.f.procedure.apply_simp) rather than run. Use Valid.f for this procedure as a module.

                                                                                                                                                                                            Gap list (batch-fix later, see TRANSFER_SKILL.md §1.6):

                                                                                                                                                                                            • GAP 1 (closed 2026-11-22): ideal_equiv's F.f guard valid p{1} = valid p{2} after sp over p, n <- x0 and x0 <- (bl, nb); EC's auto closes it, and so does ours now.

                                                                                                                                                                                            • GAP 2: EC's auto takes a one-sided sampling of a lossless distribution (r <$ dout) as lossless; ours does since 2026-11-22 (@[ec_lossless]: bdistr_expected_one, cdistr_expected_one). Left: a conseq's postcondition closed by ec_progress (EC's smt with dunifin_ll) keeps bdistr's mass: simp only [bdistr_expected_one] (two places).

                                                                                                                                                                                            • (GAP 3, fixed: after sp, hoare_auto's skip simplifies the reads through writes before it generalizes the reads, so a test's reads and the precondition's are the same values.)

                                                                                                                                                                                            • EC's have := prefix_le1 … side goals (move=> /> &hr …): by hand, the hypotheses by rename_i on the context's tail or by type (‹(0:ℤ) ≤ _›); a hypothesis picked by a typed pattern of a read (‹(localVarLens "p" _).get _ = _›) may be spelled differently from the context's, and omega then sees two atoms: name it instead.

                                                                                                                                                                                            • EC's smt selects its lemmas (domE, mem_set, valid_spec, the definition of <=) itself: our smt_close lists them (deviation, not a gap).

                                                                                                                                                                                            • GAP 3: glob M of a module over an oracle (glob IF) in the ={…} of equiv_while's invariant stays a region, where EC reads the module's variables: the variable is written out. (glob S of a concrete module is EC's since 2026-11-12, Logic/GlobWrites.lean.)

                                                                                                                                                                                            • GAP 4 (closed 2026-11-21): equiv_conseq's frame took a call of a procedure that writes nothing (F.LRO.sample, EC's proc sample(x) = {}) as writing its module's variables; the frame is now by writes, and EC's order (conseq, then inline*) is kept.

                                                                                                                                                                                            • GAP 5 (closed 2026-11-21): EC's call (: I) on two different concrete procedures (S(IF').f ~ S(Valid2).f) is equiv_call (_ : ={x…} ∧ I) (their judgment a goal), then equiv_proc (EC's form opens the callees). equiv_call (_ : ={glob IF}) on the same concrete callee falls back to the frameless rule (no footprint bound for IF's init): ={F.RO.m}.

                                                                                                                                                                                            • GAP 6 (closed 2026-11-21): the frame of equiv_call (_ : P ==> Q) was the callee module's (S(F)), not the procedure's: S(F).fi does not call F, but the call lost the oracles' maps. The frame is now by writes.

                                                                                                                                                                                            • GAP 7 (closed 2026-11-23): a fact about unmodified variables ((p, n) = parse x) was carried in the new postcondition of hoare_conseq (: _ ==> Q) and in the loop invariant; equiv_L3_L4's three loops are now EC's while I (hoare_while, with EC's frame) and its smt lists.

                                                                                                                                                                                            • GAP 8: after sp over sa, sc <- (sa +^ b, sc); x <- (sa, sc) on both sides, the two x are known equal by their components only (x{1}.1 = …, x{2}.1 = …), and the closer does not put them together: the guard x{1} \in Perm.m <=> x{2} \in Perm.m and the goals after it start with have hx : x₁ = x₂ := Prod.ext ….

                                                                                                                                                                                            • GAP 9 (closed 2026-11-23): the closer left the guard of a split loop, (a && b) = true or = false (also decide p = !false), as it was; ec_progress now takes it apart for omega where that closes the goal. (After auto_prep the guard is still decoded by hand, which ConcreteF's lemmas over the guard need.) No seq on a Hoare triple: in the rcond side goals our auto takes the code after the loop first.

                                                                                                                                                                                            • GAP 10: splitwhile's condition reads the variables of the code left only: p, which is in the conditions alone, is written with its lens.

                                                                                                                                                                                            • GAP 11 (closed 2026-11-17): inline* opens the calls of Perm behind the first port's PRIMITIVE.view (RealIndif(Sponge, Perm, D) applies Sponge to that view).

                                                                                                                                                                                            • GAP 12: phoare_call on an abstract module has the rule for lossless oracles (EC's call (: true)), not the one with an invariant (call (: invm Perm.m Perm.mi), Real_lossless). Hand-closed: Perm.f, Perm.fi are lossless in every state here.

                                                                                                                                                                                            • GAP 13 (closed 2026-11-22): in a phoare … = 1 goal, phoare_auto left a sampling's expectation of 1 in the postcondition; it reads it off now (@[ec_lossless]).

                                                                                                                                                                                            • GAP 14 (closed 2026-11-21): after auto's skip, glob D read past initializations outside D was not rewritten (sp does it); the strict auto rewrites it now (touched_set_of_le_compl by fp_disjoint).

                                                                                                                                                                                            • GAP 15: EC's conseq without a specification (conseq=> />: the postcondition without what the precondition gives on unwritten variables) has no automatic form: the postcondition is written out.

                                                                                                                                                                                            • GAP 16 (closed 2026-11-21): inlining names the two sides' locals differently (i/i0), as EC's does; sim relates them by position (EC's equality set of pairs).

                                                                                                                                                                                            • GAP 17 (closed 2026-11-20): EC's theory AdvAbsVal is Lib/EC/AdvAbsVal.lean; neg_D_concl is EC's script.

                                                                                                                                                                                            • After sp, a goal prints as the plain prhlStmt term until the next tactic (the conditions x = e it adds are not in read form); display only.

                                                                                                                                                                                            • EC's List lemmas the scripts cite (take0, size_take, nth_take, size_cat, last_nseq, …) were missing or in the first port's files under other names: Lib/EC/ListLemmas.lean.

                                                                                                                                                                                            From Ideal_equiv_valid on, the proofs are written on the strict tactics (ec_auto, ec_close, ec_progress, ec_prep: Logic/ECAutoStrict.lean, Logic/ECProgress.lean); ideal_equiv is on the older ones.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The absorbing loop of equiv_sponge extends Redo.prefixes by take (i + 1) p, a prefix it does not know. EC proves the invariant's facts on the extended map inline, in both branches of the permutation's test (smt(mem_set get_setE domE take_take size_take …) and by hand); here each is stated once.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    theorem GaudisCrypt.SHA3.Pilot.Gconcl_list.absorb_step [SLCommon.Params] {P : EC.FMap (List Common.block) SLCommon.state} {bl : List Common.block} {i : ℤ} {m m' : EC.FMap SLCommon.state SLCommon.state} {sa : Common.block} {sc : Common.capacity} (hall : SLCommon.Prefix.all_prefixes P) (hnd : ¬P.dom (EC.take (i + 1) bl)) (hget : P.get (EC.take i bl) = some (sa, sc)) (hstep : ∀ (j : ℤ), 0 ≤ j ∧ j < i → ∃ (b : Common.block) (c : Common.capacity), P.get (EC.take j bl) = some (b, c) ∧ m.get (b +^ EC.nth default bl j, c) = P.get (EC.take (j + 1) bl)) (hm : ∀ (x : SLCommon.state), m.dom x → m'.get x = m.get x) (v : SLCommon.state) (hv : m'.get (sa +^ EC.nth default bl i, sc) = some v) (j : ℤ) (hj : 0 ≤ j ∧ j < i + 1) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    ∃ (b : Common.block) (c : Common.capacity), (P.set (EC.take (i + 1) bl) v).get (EC.take j bl) = some (b, c) ∧ m'.get (b +^ EC.nth default bl j, c) = (P.set (EC.take (i + 1) bl) v).get (EC.take (j + 1) bl)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The extended map records the permutation's steps along p, up to i + 1: m' is the permutation's map after the step (m with, possibly, one more entry), v its value at the state recorded for take i p xored with the next block.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The squeezing loop of equiv_sponge runs the squeezeless sponge on format p (i + 1) when format p i is a known prefix: all its blocks but the last are known. EC proves this at each rcond and in each loop (have->: take (i1 + 1) (format bl (i + 1)) = take (i1 + 1) (format bl i); smt(all_prefixes_of_INV_real), smt(take_format size_cat size_nseq …)); here once for the blocks of p and once for the padding.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    source

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    EC.size (BlockSponge.format bl j) = EC.size bl + max 0 (j - 1)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    EC's size_cat, size_nseq on format.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    EC.take k (BlockSponge.format bl j) = EC.take k bl

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    EC's smt(take_cat take_le0 cats0): within p, a prefix of format p j is one of p.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    P.dom (EC.take (i1 + 1) (BlockSponge.format bl (i + 1)))

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    m.get (sa +^ EC.nth default l i, sc) = P.get (EC.take (i + 1) l)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    A known next prefix is the permutation's step from the current one. EC proves it inline at each use in squeeze_squeezeless's absorbing loop (have[]_[]_ hmp1 _ :=H2;have:=hmp1 _ H5 i0 _;1:smt(size_take). move=>[]b3 c3;rewrite!take_take!nth_take …, five times).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    EC.take (EC.size bl + i - 1 + 1) (BlockSponge.format bl (i + 1)) = BlockSponge.format bl (i + 1)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    EC's rewrite take_oversize;1:rewrite size_cat size_nseq ler_maxr/# at i1 = size p + i - 1: the whole of format p (i + 1).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Section Real_Ideal #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    concl (EC l. 1786) applies Gconcl.Real_Ideal to the composed distinguisher A(D), with A_lossless for its D_ll. EC's glob A(D) is glob D and C.c by definition; here the footprint of an application is bounded from above only, so {-A(D)} does not give {-D}. The pilots' Real_Ideal is therefore stated against a region for glob D (declare module … with glob R, Logic/DeclareModule.lean; exception E14), and concl gives the region of A(D) written out, R ⊔ C.c.footprint. This section's D has a region too: EC applies concl to Neg_D(D) (neg_D_concl).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Section Real_Ideal_Abs #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    EC's section, complete. Three deviations, each at its lemma: Real_lossless calls D with lossless oracles where EC keeps the invariant invm Perm.m Perm.mi (GAP 12); in Ideal_lossless the sampling behind a loop is passed by phoare_auto; neg_D_concl is EC's script with AdvAbsVal's Neg_A_Pr_minus. The section's D has a region for glob D (exception E14): concl is applied to Neg_D(D) here, and Inefficient_Real_Ideal to a distinguisher built from a declared one in SHA3Indiff.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Deviation (GAP 12): EC calls D under the invariant invm Perm.m Perm.mi, under which the permutation's sampling is lossless (useful). phoare_call on an abstract module has the rule for lossless oracles only, and here Perm.f, Perm.fi are lossless in every state (the first port's P_f_ll, P_fi_ll: a finite map missing a key misses a value). So the call is EC's call (: true), the oracles' proofs keep EC's steps without the invariant, and the calls of the permutation are not inlined: EC's inline* on the functionality's oracle is phoare_inline 0 (the sponge's call only), so that call P_f_ll applies to the permutation's calls.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The proof is EC's, with these differences. The fact EC derives inline three times (the query parsed on the left formats back to the list parsed on the right) is parse_format_of_eq_parse. In the invalid query, EC shows that the last query is already sampled by splitting off the loop's last iteration (splitwhile, rcondt, rcondf, seq on a Hoare triple); there is no seq on a Hoare triple here (GAP 9), and the loop is given the invariant "the query before i is sampled" directly. The invariant of the main loop carries what the loops do not write (GAP 15).
